title: SCOBY + Birch Sap — Stage-0 Feedstock Challenger
purpose: Test whether birch sap can serve as a reproducible feedstock for bacterial-cellulose production and whether any effect survives carbon and assimilable-nitrogen normalization.

rationale.carbon: Birch sap naturally supplies fermentable sugars, including glucose and fructose, making a BC-production route biochemically plausible.
rationale.nitrogen: Assimilable nitrogen may differ materially from canonical tea-based medium and must be measured or experimentally rescued rather than assumed.
rationale.minerals: The natural mineral/micronutrient matrix is retained as a candidate source-specific factor until controlled comparisons resolve it.
rationale.starting_pH: Birch sap starting acidity can differ from canonical SCOBY medium and must be recorded and controlled in causal comparisons.
rationale.microbiome: Native birch-sap microorganisms are a confound; source handling and microbial background must be documented.

decision_rules.if: B0 repeatedly fails to produce reproducible BC while matched controls succeed
B0 underperforms but B1 reproducibly rescues BC production
B0 underperforms but B2 reproducibly rescues BC production
B3 differs from normalized controls after carbon, N, pH and culture context are bounded
B0 independently repeats superior dry_BC_per_consumed_carbon without contamination or hidden nutrient-dose explanation

integration.existing_program_extension: GREEN_vs_BLACK becomes GREEN_vs_BLACK_vs_BIRCH only after Stage-0 production eligibility is demonstrated.
integration.next_killer_test: Run B0/B1/B2/B3 beside canonical black and green controls and determine whether carbon normalization, assimilable-N rescue, both, or neither explains birch-sap BC performance.

safety_scope: Research recipe/preregistration only. Use appropriate food/microbiology hygiene and contained culture handling. Do not interpret uncontrolled wild fermentation as a defined SCOBY result.
